title: Blink & Traffic Lights
intro: Make an LED blink, then add two more and run them like real traffic lights.

steps.title: Blink the red LED
steps.text:
Let's make the red LED blink: on for one second, off for one second, again and again.

- `pinMode(LED_RED, OUTPUT);` tells the board the red LED's pin will send power **out**.
- `digitalWrite(LED_RED, HIGH);` turns the LED **on**. `LOW` turns it **off**.
- `delay(1000);` waits 1000 milliseconds (1 second).

The `#define` lines at the top give each pin a name, so `LED_RED` means the pin your red LED is plugged into.

**Your task:** fill in the blank (`___`) so the LED turns off, then press **Run**.
hints: The blank needs the opposite of `HIGH`.

checks.label: I saw the red LED blink

steps.success: Your first blink! Every light, screen and robot starts with code like this.

steps.title: Faster!
steps.text:
The number in `delay()` is how long to wait, in milliseconds. 1000 milliseconds is one second.

**Your task:** make the LED blink much faster: change **both** delays to `200`.
hints: A smaller number means a shorter wait.

checks.label: Both delays are shorter than half a second
I saw the red LED blink faster

steps.success: Speedy! Try other numbers too. How fast can it blink before it just looks dim?

steps.title: Three lights
steps.text:
Now let's use all three LEDs. Each one needs its own `pinMode` in `setup()`, then `loop()` can turn them on and off in turn.

**Your task:** finish the code so the red, yellow and green LEDs light up one after another (each for half a second).
hints: The green LED needs `pinMode` too: what's its name in the `#define` lines?
Copy the three yellow lines and change `LED_YELLOW` to `LED_GREEN`.

checks.label: I saw all three LEDs light up in turn

steps.success: Three LEDs in a row! That's called a sequence: steps that happen one after another, in order.

steps.title: Traffic lights
steps.text: **Goal:** real traffic lights. Green for 3 seconds, yellow for 1 second, then red for 3 seconds, over and over. Only one light is on at a time.
hints: Start with green, because cars go first. Then yellow, then red.
Each light is three lines: on, wait, off. Only the `delay` numbers change.

checks.label: Green and red stay on for 3 seconds
I saw green, yellow, red, again and again

steps.success: Traffic lights, done! Real traffic lights use the same idea, with sensors to know when cars are waiting.

outro: You made real traffic lights! You used **pinMode**, **digitalWrite** and **delay** to control the timing of lights, just like the lights at an intersection.
stretch: Night mode: make the yellow light flash on and off, the way some traffic lights do late at night.
Before the light turns red, make the yellow LED flash 3 times. (Try a for loop.)
Print the light's colour to the Serial Monitor each time it changes, like "GREEN", "YELLOW", "RED".
